source: ESPN public injury report and game summaries

injuries.name: Jordan McLaughlin
injuries.short_comment: McLaughlin (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Kings.
injuries.long_comment: McLaughlin may miss his seventh game of the year. With De'Aaron Fox (shin) also questionable and Dylan Harper (hip) already sidelined, McLaughlin would be in line to receive extra minutes if he manages to suit up. However, if he's not available versus Sacramento, David Jones Garcia could see significantly more work than usual.

injuries.name: De'Aaron Fox
injuries.short_comment: Fox is questionable for Monday's game against the Kings due to a right shin contusion, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
injuries.long_comment: Fox could miss Monday's game due to a shin injury he likely picked up during Saturday's game against the Pelicans. With Dylan Harper (hip) out and Jordan McLaughlin (shoulder) questionable, the Spurs could be thin at the lead guard position, leaving more ball-handling responsibilities for Stephon Castle.

injuries.name: Dylan Harper
injuries.short_comment: Harper (hip) is expected to miss two to three weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injuries.long_comment: Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain, and San Antonio is now set to be without one of its regular guards for an extended stretch. His absence creates more backcourt minutes for the Spurs, likely most prominently for Justin Champagnie while the team waits for Tobias Harris (calf) to make his season debut. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle should see extra ball-handling duties as well.

injuries.name: Jayden Quaintance
injuries.short_comment: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
injuries.long_comment: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

injuries.name: Victor Wembanyama
injuries.short_comment: Wembanyama (back) is questionable for Monday's game against the Kings, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
injuries.long_comment: Wembanyama is dealing with lower-back tightness, leaving his status for Monday's road tilt up in the air. If he's unable to play, Luke Kornet would likely replace Wembanyama in the starting lineup, while Carter Bryant, Keldon Johnson and rookie Tarris Reed Jr. could all see a bump in minutes off the Spurs' bench.

injuries.name: Tobias Harris
injuries.short_comment: Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio.
injuries.long_comment: Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

injuries.name: Ben Simmons
injuries.short_comment: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
injuries.long_comment: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

injuries.name: Maxime Raynaud
injuries.short_comment: Raynaud (knee) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
injuries.long_comment: Raynaud continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff, suggesting he's still not close. He should be considered week-to-week moving forward.
